pluss::timeindex::date_range¶

Back to TimeIndex Factory API Reference

Signature¶

pluss::TimeIndex pluss::timeindex::date_range(
    const pluss::Timeline& start,
    const pluss::Timeline& end,
    std::string_view freq,
    std::int64_t step = 1,
    bool require_sorted = true)

Build A Regular Temporal Axis¶

date_range() starts at scalar start, advances by step units of freq, and includes end when repeated stepping lands on it exactly. It returns a one-dimensional TimeIndex directly, avoiding a temporary public Timeline at the call site.

Fixed units such as seconds, minutes, and hours advance elapsed nanoseconds. Day frequency advances civil calendar days in start’s timezone, preserving the local clock across offset changes. The result inherits the start timezone; the end value is compared as an instant.

step may have magnitude greater than one. Positive stepping is naturally non-decreasing and works with the default ordering check. Negative stepping constructs a descending range and therefore requires require_sorted=false. Zero is rejected because it cannot make progress. When step direction points away from the endpoint, the result is an empty TimeIndex.

Parameters¶

Parameter

Meaning

Default

start

Inclusive scalar first instant and source timezone

required

end

Inclusive scalar bound

required

freq

Step unit such as "S", "min", "H", or "D"

required

step

Non-zero signed count of frequency units

1

require_sorted

Require non-decreasing output before returning

true

Both endpoints must be defined scalar Timelines. NaT, non-scalar endpoints, unsupported frequencies, arithmetic overflow, and zero steps fail before a partial result is returned.

Examples¶

Example 1. Build an inclusive two-hour cadence.

auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2025-01-01T00:00:00Z");
auto end = pluss::timeline::make("2025-01-01T06:00:00Z");
auto index = pluss::timeindex::date_range(start, end, "H", 2);
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(index) << "\n";

Output¶

TimeIndex(shape=[4], tz=UTC)
[ 2025-01-01 00:00:00, 2025-01-01 02:00:00, 2025-01-01 04:00:00, 2025-01-01 06:00:00 ]

Example 2. Civil days retain the local hour across the spring offset change.

auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-09T09:00:00")
                 .tz_localize("America/Edmonton");
auto end = pluss::timeline::make("2024-03-11T09:00:00")
               .tz_localize("America/Edmonton");
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(
    pluss::timeindex::date_range(start, end, "D")) << "\n";

Output¶

TimeIndex(shape=[3], tz=America/Edmonton)
[ 2024-03-09 09:00:00, 2024-03-10 09:00:00, 2024-03-11 09:00:00 ]

Example 3. Negative stepping is available when descending index semantics are requested explicitly.

auto descending =
    pluss::timeindex::date_range(end, start, "D", -1, false);
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(descending) << "\n";

Output¶

TimeIndex(shape=[3], tz=America/Edmonton)
[ 2024-03-11 09:00:00, 2024-03-10 09:00:00, 2024-03-09 09:00:00 ]

Example 4. Leaving the default ordering check enabled rejects that descending axis.

try {
  (void)pluss::timeindex::date_range(end, start, "D", -1);
} catch (const std::exception& error) {
  std::cout << std::string_view(error.what()).substr(0,
      std::string_view(error.what()).find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

TimeIndex must be sorted (non-decreasing)

Example 5. A zero step is invalid.

try {
  (void)pluss::timeindex::date_range(start, end, "D", 0);
} catch (const std::exception& error) {
  std::cout << std::string_view(error.what()).substr(0,
      std::string_view(error.what()).find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

date_range step must be non-zero

Cost And Precision¶

Each output tick is generated exactly in signed 64-bit nanoseconds. The operation runs in O(result.size()) time and allocates one packed tick buffer. Civil-day stepping performs timezone conversion per lane; fixed-unit stepping uses checked nanosecond arithmetic.
